title.zh: 卷428 列傳二百十五 秦定三 郝光甲 郑魁士 傅振邦 邱联恩 黄开榜 陈国瑞 郭宝昌
title.en: Volume 428 Biographies 215: Qin Dingsan, Hao Guangjia, Zheng Kuishi, Fu Zhenbang, Qiu Lianen, Huang Kaibang, Chen Guorui, Guo Baochang
title.raw: 卷428 列傳二百十五 秦定三 郝光甲 郑魁士 傅振邦 邱联恩 黄开榜 陈国瑞 郭宝昌

sentences.zh: 列傳二百十五

translations.literal: Biographies 215
translations.idiomatic: Biography 215

sentences.zh: 秦定三，字竹坡，湖北興國人。

translations.literal: Qin Dingsan, styled Zhupo, was a native of Xingguo in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Dingsan, courtesy name Zhupo, came from Xingguo in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 道光六年武進士，授二等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the military examinations as a wujinshi and was appointed a second-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his military jinshi degree in the sixth year of Daoguang and was appointed a second-class imperial guardsman.

sentences.zh: 出為廣西桂林營游擊，洊擢貴州鎮遠鎮總兵。

translations.literal: On leaving the capital he became garrison commander of the Guilin camp in Guangxi and was repeatedly promoted to commander-in-chief of the Zhenyuan garrison in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving the capital he served as colonel of the Guilin camp in Guangxi, and in due course rose to commander-in-chief of the Zhenyuan garrison in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十年，平湖南李沅發之亂，賜號愨勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he pacified the rebellion of Li Yuanfa in Hunan and was granted the title Ke Yong Batu'eru.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he helped put down Li Yuanfa's rebellion in Hunan and was awarded the title Loyal and Brave Batooru.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，率貴州、雲南兵赴廣西剿匪，克武宣三里墟賊營。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he led Guizhou and Yunnan troops to Guangxi to suppress bandits and captured the rebel camp at Sanli Market in Wuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he led troops from Guizhou and Yunnan into Guangxi against the rebels and took their camp at Sanli Market in Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 進剿象州，以賊竄逸，坐褫花翎，降三級留任。

translations.literal: Advancing to suppress Xiangzhou, because the rebels slipped away he was punished by stripping his peacock feather, demoted three ranks, and retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: When he pressed the attack on Xiangzhou the rebels broke away, and he was stripped of his peacock feather, demoted three ranks, and kept on in his post.

sentences.zh: 尋連破賊馬鞍山、竹園村，復之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he repeatedly defeated the rebels at Ma'anshan and Zhuyuan Village and had his honors restored.
translations.idiomatic: He soon won successive victories at Ma'anshan and Zhuyuan Village, and his honors were restored.

sentences.zh: 偕副都統烏蘭泰破賊新墟，又奪雙髻山、豬仔峽要隘，被嘉獎。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Commander-in-Chief Ulan Tai he defeated the rebels at Xin Market, then seized the strategic passes at Shuangji Hill and Zhuzai Gorge and was commended.
translations.idiomatic: Along with Vice Commander-in-Chief Ulan Tai he routed the rebels at Xin Market, then took the strategic passes at Shuangji Hill and Zhuzai Gorge and received imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 又擊賊於永安州，力戰受傷。

translations.literal: He again attacked the rebels at Yong'an Prefecture, fought fiercely, and was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the rebels again at Yong'an Prefecture, battled hard, and was wounded in action.

sentences.zh: 二年，破水竇賊壘，賊棄永安潰圍走，擒賊首洪大泉。

translations.literal: In the second year he stormed the rebel fort at Shuidou; the rebels abandoned Yong'an and broke out in flight, and the rebel leader Hong Daquan was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he stormed the rebel stronghold at Shuidou; the rebels abandoned Yong'an and fled the siege, and their leader Hong Daquan was taken.

sentences.zh: 賊趨桂林，定三偕烏蘭泰追之。

translations.literal: The rebels moved toward Guilin, and Dingsan together with Ulan Tai pursued them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels turned toward Guilin, Dingsan and Ulan Tai gave chase.

sentences.zh: 急不暇結營而戰，定三止之，勿聽，烏蘭泰以傷歿。

translations.literal: In their haste they fought without time to make camp; Dingsan tried to stop them but was not heeded, and Ulan Tai died of his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked in such haste that they had no time to pitch camp; Dingsan urged restraint but was ignored, and Ulan Tai died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 定三代將其軍，克花礄。

translations.literal: Dingsan took command of his army in his stead and captured Huajiao.
translations.idiomatic: Dingsan then took over his command and captured Huajiao.

sentences.zh: 桂林尋解圍，以保守省城被優敘。

translations.literal: Guilin was soon relieved, and for defending the provincial capital he received preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Guilin was soon relieved, and he earned special commendation for having held the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 追賊入湖南，破賊於道州桃花井、五里亭、龍安橋，進援長沙。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rebels into Hunan, he defeated them at Taohuajing, Wuliting, and Long'an Bridge in Daozhou and advanced to relieve Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels into Hunan, routed them at Taohuajing, Wuliting, and Long'an Bridge in Daozhou, and marched to relieve Changsha.

sentences.zh: 總兵和春營妙高峰，為賊所圍，定三分兵襲賊營，得解。

translations.literal: Major General Hechun was encamped at Miaogaofeng and was surrounded by rebels; Dingsan divided his force to strike the rebel camp and secured his relief.
translations.idiomatic: Major General Hechun's camp at Miaogaofeng was surrounded; Dingsan split his force, raided the rebel camp, and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 尋賊竄岳州，定三坐不能遏賊，革職留任。

translations.literal: Soon the rebels fled to Yuezhou; Dingsan was punished for failing to check them, dismissed from office but retained on duty.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels soon slipped away to Yuezhou, Dingsan was cashiered for failing to stop them but kept on in the field.

sentences.zh: 進援武昌，戰於洪山。

translations.literal: He advanced to relieve Wuchang and fought at Hongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to relieve Wuchang and fought at Hongshan.

sentences.zh: 三年，賊浮江東下，向榮率大軍由陸路追之，令和春及定三為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the third year the rebels sailed down the river; Xiang Rong led the main army in pursuit overland and ordered Hechun and Dingsan to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the rebels sailed downriver; Xiang Rong led the main force in pursuit by land and placed Hechun and Dingsan in the van.

sentences.zh: 甫至九江，而江寧已陷。

translations.literal: They had only just reached Jiujiang when Jiangning had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: They had scarcely reached Jiujiang when Jiangning fell.

sentences.zh: 踰月大軍始至，迭戰城下，賊堅壁以拒。

translations.literal: After more than a month the main army arrived; they fought repeatedly below the walls while the rebels held firm behind their defenses.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month passed before the main army arrived; they fought again and again beneath the walls while the rebels held fast behind their defenses.

sentences.zh: 四年，賊分黨陷廬州，和春疏調定三及鄭魁士率所部往助剿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year rebel detachments seized Luzhou; Hechun memorialized to transfer Dingsan and Zheng Kuishi with their troops to assist in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year rebel bands took Luzhou, and Hechun requested that Dingsan and Zheng Kuishi bring their troops to help suppress them.

sentences.zh: 時廬州久為賊踞，旁縣並陷，定三連戰破賊，复六安，屯三角井。

translations.literal: At that time Luzhou had long been held by rebels and neighboring counties had all fallen; Dingsan fought repeatedly, defeated the rebels, recovered Lu'an, and encamped at Sanjiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou had been in rebel hands for some time and the surrounding counties had fallen; Dingsan won a series of victories, recovered Lu'an, and encamped at Sanjiaojing.

sentences.zh: 會江寧賊分黨入安徽，圖北犯，以援畿南竄匪，道經舒城；

translations.literal: Meanwhile rebel detachments from Jiangning entered Anhui intending a northern thrust to aid the roving bandits south of the capital, passing by way of Shucheng;
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile rebel forces from Jiangning entered Anhui on a northern thrust to support bandits south of the capital, marching by way of Shucheng;

sentences.zh: 賊首羅大綱、石達開、胡以晄、秦日昌等合眾數万，四路來撲。

translations.literal: the rebel leaders Luo Dagang, Shi Dakai, Hu Yiliang, Qin Richang, and others gathered tens of thousands and attacked from four directions.
translations.idiomatic: the rebel leaders Luo Dagang, Shi Dakai, Hu Yiliang, Qin Richang, and others massed tens of thousands of men and assailed him from four directions.

sentences.zh: 定三所部僅二千，堅守十餘日，陣斬羅大綱，賊始挫，引去。

translations.literal: Dingsan's force numbered only two thousand; he held firm for more than ten days, killed Luo Dagang in battle, and the rebels were checked and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Dingsan had only two thousand men under him; he held out for more than ten days, killed Luo Dagang in battle, and the rebels finally gave way and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 定三集團勇攻舒城，悉破城外賊壘，又伺賊出截擊，連破之。

translations.literal: Dingsan gathered local militia to attack Shucheng, destroyed all the rebel forts outside the walls, and when the rebels came out ambushed and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Dingsan rallied local militia against Shucheng, destroyed every rebel fort outside the walls, and whenever the rebels sallied forth he cut them off and beat them back again and again.

sentences.zh: 圍之數月，六年，賊營火藥自焚，乘其亂，薄城奮攻，梯而登，遂復舒城，殲賊四千餘，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: After besieging it for months, in the sixth year the rebels' powder stores ignited by themselves; seizing the confusion he pressed the assault, scaled the walls, recovered Shucheng, and destroyed more than four thousand rebels; he was granted a hereditary rank as Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted months; in the sixth year the rebels' powder stores exploded by accident, and in the confusion he pressed the assault, scaled the walls, and retook Shucheng, killing more than four thousand rebels; he was granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 進屯軍鋪，賊自廬江、桐城分路來犯，定三往來馳擊，大破之，复五河、廬江二縣。

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped at Junpu; rebels came from Lujiang and Tongcheng by separate routes, and Dingsan rode back and forth to strike them, inflicting a great defeat and recovering the two counties of Wuhe and Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Junpu; when rebels came against him from Lujiang and Tongcheng by separate routes, Dingsan rode back and forth to meet them, won a crushing victory, and recovered Wuhe and Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 進規桐城，奪小關、下關、白河嶺諸隘，屯陳家鋪。

translations.literal: He advanced against Tongcheng, seized the passes at Xiaoguan, Xiaguan, and Baiheling, and encamped at Chenjiapu.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the campaign against Tongcheng, took the passes at Xiaoguan, Xiaguan, and Baiheling, and encamped at Chenjiapu.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，賊由安慶來援，定三血戰十八日，賊乃退。

translations.literal: That winter rebels came from Anqing to relieve the city; Dingsan fought bitterly for eighteen days before the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That winter rebels marched from Anqing to relieve the city; Dingsan fought them bitterly for eighteen days until they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又破賊於桐城北門外，毀其城樓。

translations.literal: He again defeated the rebels outside the north gate of Tongcheng and destroyed their gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the rebels again outside Tongcheng's north gate and destroyed their gate tower.

sentences.zh: 捻匪擾河南，詔定三赴蒙城、亳州會剿，以鄭魁士代任桐城軍事。

translations.literal: Nian bandits harassed Henan; an edict ordered Dingsan to Mengcheng and Bozhou for joint suppression, with Zheng Kuishi to replace him in the Tongcheng command.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian bandits raided Henan, the court ordered Dingsan to Mengcheng and Bozhou for a joint campaign and placed Zheng Kuishi in charge at Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 巡撫福濟疏言定三圍攻方得手，留之。

translations.literal: Governor Fu Ji memorialized that Dingsan's siege was just succeeding and asked that he be kept there.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fu Ji reported that Dingsan's siege was on the verge of success and asked that he be kept in place.

sentences.zh: 改以魁士援北路，而魁士軍已至。

translations.literal: The plan was changed so that Kuishi would reinforce the northern route, but Kuishi's army had already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Kuishi was reassigned to reinforce the northern front, but his army had already arrived on the scene.

sentences.zh: 定三初與魁士同列，及和春赴江南督師，魁士會辦安徽軍務，權位出定三上，又因爭餉，定三心不平，上疏劾之。

translations.literal: Dingsan had originally been Kuishi's equal in rank, but when Hechun went south to command in Jiangnan, Kuishi was made co-director of Anhui military affairs with authority above Dingsan; because of disputes over rations Dingsan was resentful and memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Dingsan had once been Kuishi's peer, but after Hechun went south to take command in Jiangnan, Kuishi was made co-director of Anhui military affairs with authority over him; quarrels over supplies bred resentment, and Dingsan memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 福濟所恃惟兩軍，難左右袒，軍飢且渙。

translations.literal: Fu Ji relied on these two armies alone and could favor neither side; the troops were hungry and disorganized.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ji depended on these two armies alone and could not take sides between them; the troops went hungry and discipline frayed.

sentences.zh: 七年春，賊又陷廬江，進犯桐城。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year the rebels again took Lujiang and advanced against Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year the rebels seized Lujiang again and marched on Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 官軍為所圍，不戰而潰，坐褫翎頂。

translations.literal: The government troops were surrounded and collapsed without fighting; he was punished by stripping his insignia.
translations.idiomatic: The government force was surrounded and broke without a fight; he was stripped of his insignia for it.

sentences.zh: 文宗知定三頻年苦戰，敗非其罪，原之，故薄譴，命赴江南大營，隸和春軍，屯句容。

translations.literal: The Wenzong Emperor knew that Dingsan had fought bitterly for years and that the defeat was not his fault, and pardoned him, hence the light punishment; he was ordered to the great camp in Jiangnan, placed under Hechun's command, and stationed at Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong knew Dingsan had fought hard for years and that the defeat was not his fault, and pardoned him with a light punishment; he was sent to the great camp in Jiangnan under Hechun and stationed at Jurong.

sentences.zh: 大軍方攻鎮江，令移駐溧水以遏援賊。

translations.literal: The main army was then attacking Zhenjiang, and he was ordered to move his station to Lishui to block relieving rebels.
translations.idiomatic: While the main army was attacking Zhenjiang, he was ordered to move to Lishui to block rebel reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於軍，詔念前勞，依例賜卹，諡恭武。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died in camp; an edict recalled his former service, granted the usual posthumous pension, and gave him the posthumous title Gongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in camp; the court honored his long service with the usual pension and posthumous title Gongwu.

sentences.zh: 郝光甲，直隸任丘人。

translations.literal: Hao Guangjia was a native of Renqiu in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Guangjia came from Renqiu in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 道光十八年一甲一名武進士，授頭等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Daoguang he took first place among military graduates of the first class and was appointed a first-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Daoguang he finished first in the top class of the military examinations and was appointed a first-class imperial guardsman.

sentences.zh: 出為山東撫標中軍參將，巡撫李僡薦之，超擢陝安鎮總兵。

translations.literal: On leaving the capital he became brigade general of the central army of the Shandong provincial garrison; Governor Li Huan recommended him and he was promoted out of turn to commander-in-chief of the Shan'an garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving the capital he served as brigade general of the Shandong provincial garrison; Governor Li Huan recommended him, and he was promoted out of turn to commander-in-chief of the Shan'an garrison.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，率陝、甘兵援山東，從解懷慶圍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he led Shaanxi and Gansu troops to aid Shandong and helped lift the siege of Huaiqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he led troops from Shaanxi and Gansu to Shandong and helped raise the siege of Huaiqing.

sentences.zh: 追賊至山西，破之於平陽。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rebels into Shanxi, he defeated them at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels into Shanxi and defeated them at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 賊入畿輔，光甲從勝保追剿，陝甘總督舒興阿勦賊河南，互相爭調，光甲以擅自移營褫職。

translations.literal: When the rebels entered the metropolitan region Guangjia followed Senggelinqin in pursuit; Shaanxi-Gansu Governor Shu Xing'a was suppressing rebels in Henan, and they disputed over transfers; Guangjia was dismissed for moving camp without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels entered the metropolitan region, Guangjia followed Senggelinqin in pursuit; Shaanxi-Gansu Governor Shu Xing'a was fighting rebels in Henan, and the two quarreled over troop assignments; Guangjia was dismissed for moving his camp without orders.

sentences.zh: 尋隨舒興阿援安徽，其軍改隸秦定三。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Shu Xing'a to relieve Anhui, and his army was placed under Qin Dingsan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Shu Xing'a to Anhui, and his force was placed under Qin Dingsan.

sentences.zh: 戰舒城，迭破賊，詔予三品頂戴，署陝安鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Fighting at Shucheng he repeatedly defeated the rebels; an edict granted him a third-rank insignia and acting appointment as commander-in-chief of the Shan'an garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At Shucheng he won repeated victories; the court granted him third-rank insignia and acting command of the Shan'an garrison.

sentences.zh: 從克廬州，复舒城，复總兵頂戴，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He took part in capturing Luzhou and recovering Shucheng, had his major-general insignia restored, and was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He helped capture Luzhou and recover Shucheng, had his major-general insignia restored, and was awarded a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 尋調赴河南剿捻，誤往徐州，被劾，革職留營。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Henan to suppress the Nian, but mistakenly went to Xuzhou, was impeached, dismissed from office, and kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to Henan against the Nian but went to Xuzhou by mistake, was impeached, cashiered, and kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 擊潁州捻匪於江集，擒捻首王鳳林。

translations.literal: He attacked Nian bandits from Yingzhou at Jiangji and captured the Nian leader Wang Fenglin.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Nian bandits from Yingzhou at Jiangji and captured their leader Wang Fenglin.

sentences.zh: 復以調赴蒙城遲延，降二級。

translations.literal: Again, for delay in moving to Mengcheng as ordered, he was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted two ranks for again being slow to march to Mengcheng as ordered.

sentences.zh: 七年，援桐城，兵敗，歿於陣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, relieving Tongcheng, his army was defeated and he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, while marching to relieve Tongcheng, his force was beaten and he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 詔復原官，依總兵賜卹，予騎都尉世職，諡武節。

translations.literal: An edict restored his former rank, granted the pension due a major general, awarded a hereditary rank as Cavalry Commandant, and gave him the posthumous title Wujie.
translations.idiomatic: The court restored his former rank, granted a major general's pension, awarded the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant, and gave him the posthumous title Wujie.

sentences.zh: 鄭魁士，直隸萬全人。

translations.literal: Zheng Kuishi was a native of Wanquan in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Kuishi came from Wanquan in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 由行伍洊擢湖南提標守備。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was repeatedly promoted to garrison commander of the Hunan provincial brigade.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to become garrison commander of the Hunan provincial brigade.

sentences.zh: 道光三十年，平李沅發之亂，擢鎮筸鎮標都司。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he helped pacify the rebellion of Li Yuanfa and was promoted to battalion commander of the Zhenqian garrison standard.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he helped put down Li Yuanfa's rebellion and was promoted to battalion commander of the Zhenqian garrison.

sentences.zh: 從提督向榮赴廣西剿匪，屢捷，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He followed Regional Commander Xiang Rong to Guangxi to suppress bandits, won repeated victories, and was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Regional Commander Xiang Rong to Guangxi against the rebels, won repeated victories, and was awarded a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 擢湖南九谿營游擊，以參將升用。

translations.literal: He was promoted to colonel of the Jiuxi camp in Hunan and advanced to brigade general.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to colonel of the Jiuxi camp in Hunan and then to brigade general.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，守桂林，援長沙，擢副將，賜號沙拉瑪巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he defended Guilin and relieved Changsha, was promoted to deputy commander, and was granted the title Shalama Batu'eru.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he held Guilin and relieved Changsha, was promoted to deputy commander, and was awarded the title Shalama Batooru.

sentences.zh: 援武昌，遂從向榮追賊沿江東下。

translations.literal: He relieved Wuchang and then followed Xiang Rong in pursuit of the rebels down the river.
translations.idiomatic: After relieving Wuchang he followed Xiang Rong in pursuit of the rebels downriver.

sentences.zh: 以違軍令被劾，褫職留營。

translations.literal: For violating military orders he was impeached, dismissed from office, and kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached for disobeying orders, cashiered, and kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 尋戰江寧有功，給都司翎頂。

translations.literal: Soon, for merit in fighting at Jiangning, he was given the insignia of a battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He soon earned merit at Jiangning and was given battalion-commander insignia.

sentences.zh: 四年，提督和春調率所部赴廬州，進攻屢捷，復其職。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Regional Commander Hechun transferred him with his troops to Luzhou; his attacks won repeated victories and his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Regional Commander Hechun took him and his troops to Luzhou; his attacks kept succeeding and his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋署安徽壽春鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made acting commander-in-chief of the Shouchun garrison in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting commander-in-chief of the Shouchun garrison in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 廬州數縣皆陷，府城賊眾糧足，殊死守。

translations.literal: Several counties around Luzhou had fallen; in the prefectural city the rebels were numerous and well supplied and defended it stubbornly.
translations.idiomatic: Several counties around Luzhou had fallen; inside the prefectural city the rebels were numerous, well supplied, and defended it to the last.

sentences.zh: 和春一軍倚魁士及秦定三二人，定三分兵攻舒城；

translations.literal: Hechun's army relied on Kuishi and Qin Dingsan; Dingsan divided his force to attack Shucheng;
translations.idiomatic: Hechun's army depended on Kuishi and Qin Dingsan; Dingsan detached troops to attack Shucheng;

sentences.zh: 而廬州軍事專恃魁士。

translations.literal: but the Luzhou campaign depended solely on Kuishi.
translations.idiomatic: while the Luzhou campaign rested entirely on Kuishi.

sentences.zh: 圍攻歷年餘，安慶、江寧援賊屢來援，皆擊走。

translations.literal: The siege lasted more than a year; relieving rebels from Anqing and Jiangning came repeatedly and were all driven off.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted more than a year; rebel relief columns from Anqing and Jiangning came again and again, and each time he drove them off.

sentences.zh: 至五年冬，攻愈急，魁士潛至城下以雲梯登城克之。

translations.literal: By the winter of the fifth year the assault grew fiercer; Kuishi stole up to the walls, scaled them with cloud ladders, and captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: By the winter of the fifth year the assault had grown desperate; Kuishi stole up to the walls, scaled them on siege ladders, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 被優敘，加提督銜。

translations.literal: He received preferential commendation and was given the brevet rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He earned special commendation and was given brevet rank as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 六年春，追賊至三河，焚其巢，而捻匪日熾。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year he pursued the rebels to Sanhe and burned their lair, but the Nian bandits grew daily stronger.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he pursued the rebels to Sanhe and burned their base, even as the Nian grew stronger by the day.

sentences.zh: 魁士率兵赴宿州擊破之，乃分路竄入河南境。

translations.literal: Kuishi led troops to Suzhou and defeated them, whereupon they split into bands and fled into Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Kuishi marched to Suzhou and routed them, and they scattered in bands into Henan.

sentences.zh: 巡撫英桂疏請魁士赴援永城，和春方倚辦皖賊，疏留，令往來策應。

translations.literal: Governor Ying Gui memorialized asking that Kuishi go to relieve Yongcheng; Hechun was then relying on him against Anhui rebels and memorialized to keep him, ordering him to move back and forth in support.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ying Gui asked that Kuishi march to relieve Yongcheng; Hechun, who still needed him against the Anhui rebels, asked to keep him and ordered him to shuttle back and forth in support.

sentences.zh: 於是迭擊捻匪於懷遠茅塘集、河溜等處，擒其酋褚淀等四十餘人。

translations.literal: He then repeatedly attacked Nian bandits at Maotangji in Huaiyuan, Heliu, and other places, capturing more than forty of their chiefs including Chu Dian.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck the Nian again and again at Maotangji in Huaiyuan, Heliu, and elsewhere, capturing more than forty of their chiefs, including Chu Dian.

sentences.zh: 又破之於蒙城，焚其積聚。

translations.literal: He again defeated them at Mengcheng and burned their stores.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them again at Mengcheng and burned their stockpiles.

sentences.zh: 駐守懷遠賊分隊來犯，魁士被圍，力戰，身被二十餘創，卒破賊，解圍去，詔嘉其勇，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: While stationed at Huaiyuan a rebel detachment attacked; Kuishi was surrounded, fought fiercely, received more than twenty wounds, finally broke the rebels, and lifted the siege; an edict praised his valor and granted him a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: While he was stationed at Huaiyuan a rebel detachment attacked; Kuishi was surrounded, fought on despite more than twenty wounds, finally broke the enemy, and raised the siege; the court praised his courage and granted him a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 又督團練敗賊於太和。

translations.literal: He also directed local militia to defeat the rebels at Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He also led local militia to defeat the rebels at Taihe.

sentences.zh: 會和春督師江南，詔安徽軍務以魁士繼任，會同巡撫福濟督辦，實授壽春鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When Hechun took command in Jiangnan, an edict placed Anhui military affairs in Kuishi's hands to succeed him, jointly supervised with Governor Fu Ji, and he was formally appointed commander-in-chief of the Shouchun garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Hechun took command in Jiangnan, the court put Anhui military affairs in Kuishi's hands, with Governor Fu Ji as his partner, and formally appointed him commander-in-chief of the Shouchun garrison.

sentences.zh: 迭克舒城、廬江、無為，下部優敘，頒賜御用衣服及珍物。

translations.literal: He successively recovered Shucheng, Lujiang, and Wuwei; the ministry gave him preferential commendation and bestowed imperial garments and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Shucheng, Lujiang, and Wuwei in turn; the ministry commended him specially and the court bestowed imperial garments and treasures.

sentences.zh: 又以魁士躬冒鋒鏑，被創甚劇，特詔嘉獎，賜藥調治。

translations.literal: Because Kuishi had personally braved the blades and been severely wounded, a special edict praised him and granted medicine for his recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had faced the blades himself and been badly wounded, a special edict praised him and sent medicine for his recovery.

sentences.zh: 先後分兵復和州、潛山。

translations.literal: In succession he detached troops to recover Hezhou and Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: He then detached troops to recover Hezhou and Qianshan in turn.

sentences.zh: 先是秦定三攻桐城，賊堅守不下，魁士往會剿，迭戰，並擊退援賊。

translations.literal: Earlier Qin Dingsan had attacked Tongcheng but the rebels held firm and the city would not fall; Kuishi went to join the campaign, fought repeatedly, and drove off relieving rebels as well.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qin Dingsan had besieged Tongcheng without success; Kuishi joined the campaign, fought battle after battle, and drove off the relief columns as well.

sentences.zh: 時悍賊石達開往來桐城、安慶，勢甚張；

translations.literal: At that time the formidable rebel Shi Dakai moved back and forth between Tongcheng and Anqing and his power was very great;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the formidable rebel Shi Dakai ranged between Tongcheng and Anqing with great force;

sentences.zh: 又勾通捻匪，蔓延皖、豫之間。

translations.literal: he also colluded with Nian bandits and spread disorder between Anhui and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: he also colluded with the Nian, and trouble spread across Anhui and Henan.

sentences.zh: 詔秦定三移兵蒙城剿捻，尋又留攻桐城，以魁士代之，會同河南巡撫英桂節制三省剿捻之兵；

translations.literal: An edict ordered Qin Dingsan to move his troops to Mengcheng to suppress the Nian, then again kept him at Tongcheng and replaced him with Kuishi to join Henan Governor Ying Gui in commanding the three provinces' Nian-suppression forces;
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Qin Dingsan to Mengcheng against the Nian, then kept him at Tongcheng and put Kuishi in his place, with Henan Governor Ying Gui commanding the three-province Nian campaign;

sentences.zh: 而桐城兵事方棘，福濟复疏留不遣。

translations.literal: but the Tongcheng situation was critical and Fu Ji again memorialized to keep him from being sent away.
translations.idiomatic: but Tongcheng was still in crisis, and Fu Ji again memorialized to keep him from leaving.

sentences.zh: 值歲荒餉匱，定三軍原取給地方捐給，魁士兵至，悉取轉供。

translations.literal: It happened to be a year of famine and scarce rations; Dingsan's army had originally been supplied by local contributions, but when Kuishi's troops arrived they took everything and diverted it to themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Famine had emptied the granaries; Dingsan's army had lived on local contributions, but when Kuishi's troops arrived they seized everything for themselves.

sentences.zh: 定三疏爭，福濟一無措置，兩軍遂成水火。

translations.literal: Dingsan memorialized in protest; Fu Ji did nothing at all, and the two armies became irreconcilable.
translations.idiomatic: Dingsan protested in a memorial; Fu Ji did nothing, and the two armies became bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 詔促魁士速赴蒙城，亦迄未行。

translations.literal: An edict urged Kuishi to hurry to Mengcheng, but in the end he still did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Kuishi to hurry to Mengcheng, but he never went.

sentences.zh: 七年春，廬江、潛山連陷，賊由安慶大舉來犯，城賊突出，官軍飢疲不相顧，不戰潰圍而走。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year Lujiang and Qianshan fell in succession; rebels came in force from Anqing, the rebels in the city sallied out, and the government troops, hungry and exhausted and heedless of one another, broke and fled the siege without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year Lujiang and Qianshan fell one after another; rebels marched in force from Anqing, the garrison sallied out, and the government troops—hungry, exhausted, and no longer acting as one—broke and fled without a fight.

sentences.zh: 於是詔褫魁士翎頂，罷其剿捻會辦，歸福濟節制。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict stripped Kuishi of his insignia, removed him as co-director of Nian suppression, and placed him under Fu Ji's command.
translations.idiomatic: The court stripped Kuishi of his insignia, removed him as co-director of the Nian campaign, and placed him under Fu Ji.

sentences.zh: 退保廬州，粵、捻各匪會合來犯，魁士迎擊挫之，复翎頂。

translations.literal: He withdrew to defend Luzhou; Cantonese and Nian bandits joined forces to attack, and Kuishi met them and checked them, and his insignia was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back to defend Luzhou; Cantonese rebels and Nian bandits joined to attack, Kuishi met them and beat them back, and his insignia was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋克桃鎮、派河，進扼全椒、滁州以杜北竄。

translations.literal: Soon he captured Taozhen and Paihe and advanced to hold Quanjiao and Chuzhou to block a northern flight.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took Taozhen and Paihe and advanced to hold Quanjiao and Chuzhou against a northern breakout.

sentences.zh: 八年，調赴江南大營，授浙江提督，督辦寧國軍務。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to the great camp in Jiangnan, appointed regional commander of Zhejiang, and charged with directing military affairs in Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was sent to the great camp in Jiangnan, made regional commander of Zhejiang, and put in charge of military affairs at Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 九年，克灣沚，進剿貴池、南陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he captured Wanzhi and advanced to suppress Guichi and Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he took Wanzhi and pressed the campaign against Guichi and Nanling.

sentences.zh: 尋命駐防高淳、東壩。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to garrison Gaochun and Dongba.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to garrison Gaochun and Dongba.

sentences.zh: 十年，以傷病乞假，詔斥屢次退卻，以總兵降補。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, on grounds of wounds and illness he asked for leave; an edict rebuked his repeated withdrawals and demoted him to major general by reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he asked for leave because of wounds and illness; the court rebuked his repeated retreats and demoted him to major general.

sentences.zh: 從漕運總督袁甲三勦賊，授甘肅寧夏鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He followed Grain Transport Governor Yuan Jiasan in suppressing rebels and was appointed commander-in-chief of the Ningxia garrison in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Grain Transport Governor Yuan Jiasan against the rebels and was appointed commander-in-chief of the Ningxia garrison in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以病罷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was dismissed on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was dismissed because of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋召來京候簡。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was summoned to the capital to await appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to the capital to await a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 同治五年，捻匪北犯，命赴直隸東路協剿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi the Nian bandits raided northward, and he was ordered to Zhili's eastern front for joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tongzhi, when the Nian raided northward, he was ordered to the eastern front in Zhili for a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 六年，署直隸提督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made acting regional commander of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as acting regional commander of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 八年，乞病歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he asked to retire home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he retired home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year.

sentences.zh: 大學士李鴻章疏陳魁士久於軍事，堅苦剛毅，疊受重傷，詔依例賜卹，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang memorialized that Kuishi had long served in the military, was steadfast, tough, and resolute, and had repeatedly suffered severe wounds; an edict granted the usual pension and gave him the posthumous title Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang reported that Kuishi had spent his life in the army, was steadfast and resolute, and had been badly wounded again and again; the court granted the usual pension and the posthumous title Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 傅振邦，山東昌邑人。

translations.literal: Fu Zhenbang was a native of Changyi in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhenbang came from Changyi in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光十六年武進士，授三等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Daoguang he passed the military examinations as a wujinshi and was appointed a third-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his military jinshi degree in the sixteenth year of Daoguang and was appointed a third-class imperial guardsman.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，出為湖南長沙協中軍都司，署鎮筸游擊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, on leaving the capital, he became battalion commander of the central army of the Changsha garrison in Hunan and acted as colonel of the Zhenqian garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he left the capital to serve as battalion commander of the Changsha garrison in Hunan and acted as colonel of the Zhenqian garrison.

sentences.zh: 三十年，從平新寧土匪李沅發，受槍傷，賜花翎，實授游擊。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he took part in pacifying the bandit Li Yuanfa in Xinning, was wounded by gunfire, was granted a peacock feather, and was formally appointed colonel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he helped put down the bandit Li Yuanfa in Xinning, was shot, was awarded a peacock feather, and was formally appointed colonel.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，赴援桂林。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he went to relieve Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he marched to relieve Guilin.

sentences.zh: 三年，從向榮追賊抵江南，擢湖南撫標中軍參將。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Xiang Rong in pursuit of the rebels to Jiangnan and was promoted to brigade general of the central army of the Hunan provincial garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Xiang Rong in pursuit of the rebels into Jiangnan and was promoted to brigade general of the Hunan provincial garrison.

sentences.zh: 以圍攻江寧功，賜號綽克托巴圖魯。

translations.literal: For merit in besieging Jiangning he was granted the title Zhuoketuo Batu'eru.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in the siege of Jiangning he was awarded the title Zhuoketuo Batooru.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢貴州定廣協副將，署江蘇徐州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to deputy commander of the Dingguang garrison in Guizhou and acted as commander-in-chief of the Xuzhou garrison in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to deputy commander of the Dingguang garrison in Guizhou and acted as commander-in-chief of the Xuzhou garrison in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 賊由蕪湖犯東壩，陷高淳。

translations.literal: Rebels came from Wuhu against Dongba and took Gaochun.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels advanced from Wuhu against Dongba and captured Gaochun.

sentences.zh: 向榮令迎擊敗之，復其城。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong ordered him to meet and defeat them, and he recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong ordered him to meet the attack, and he defeated the rebels and recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 又偕鄧紹良克太平府，偪秣陵關，破賊於採石磯。

translations.literal: He also joined Deng Shaoliang in capturing Taiping Prefecture, pressed toward Moling Pass, and defeated the rebels at Caishiji.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Deng Shaoliang in taking Taiping Prefecture, pressed toward Moling Pass, and routed the rebels at Caishiji.

sentences.zh: 六年，蒞徐州署任。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he took up his acting post at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he assumed his acting command at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 捻酋張洛行、夏白、任乾圍宿州，振邦敗之夾溝、符離，解城圍。

translations.literal: The Nian chiefs Zhang Luoxing, Xia Bai, and Ren Qian besieged Suzhou; Zhenbang defeated them at Jiagou and Fuli and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian chiefs Zhang Luoxing, Xia Bai, and Ren Qian besieged Suzhou, Zhenbang defeated them at Jiagou and Fuli and raised the siege.

sentences.zh: 再敗張洛行於瓦子口，毀其巢。

translations.literal: He again defeated Zhang Luoxing at Wazikou and destroyed his lair.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Zhang Luoxing again at Wazikou and destroyed his base.

sentences.zh: 擊退蒙城賊於灘口。

translations.literal: He drove off the rebels from Mengcheng at Tankou.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the Mengcheng rebels back at Tankou.

sentences.zh: 又偕伊興額破捻酋紀學中、王得六於永城鐵佛寺，毀柳集、臨渙集賊巢，擒紀學中，實授徐州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He also joined Yi Xing'e in defeating the Nian chiefs Ji Xuezhong and Wang Deliu at the Iron Buddha Temple in Yongcheng, destroyed the rebel lairs at Liuji and Linhuanji, captured Ji Xuezhong, and was formally appointed commander-in-chief of the Xuzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Yi Xing'e in defeating the Nian chiefs Ji Xuezhong and Wang Deliu at the Iron Buddha Temple in Yongcheng, destroyed their bases at Liuji and Linhuanji, captured Ji Xuezhong, and was formally appointed commander-in-chief of the Xuzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 會江南大營失利，命振邦馳援。

translations.literal: When the great camp in Jiangnan suffered defeat, Zhenbang was ordered to hurry to its relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the great camp in Jiangnan was defeated, Zhenbang was ordered to hurry to its relief.

sentences.zh: 偕總兵明安泰、秦如虎破賊東壩，進攻溧水。

translations.literal: Together with Major Generals Ming Antai and Qin Ruhu he defeated the rebels at Dongba and advanced to attack Lishui.
translations.idiomatic: With Major Generals Ming Antai and Qin Ruhu he routed the rebels at Dongba and advanced on Lishui.

sentences.zh: 七年，克之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he took the city.

sentences.zh: 又破賊湖墅，追至龍都，偕張國樑克句容，加提督銜。

translations.literal: He again defeated the rebels at Hushu, pursued them to Longdu, joined Zhang Guoliang in capturing Jurong, and was given the brevet rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels again at Hushu, pursued them to Longdu, joined Zhang Guoliang in taking Jurong, and was given brevet rank as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 八年，援寧國，拔灣沚、黃池，郡城解嚴。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he relieved Ningguo, recovered Wanzhi and Huangchi, and the prefectural city was relieved from siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he relieved Ningguo, recovered Wanzhi and Huangchi, and the prefectural seat was no longer under siege.

sentences.zh: 四月，回軍徐州，命幫辦袁甲三軍務。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he returned his army to Xuzhou and was ordered to assist in Yuan Jiasan's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he returned to Xuzhou and was ordered to assist Yuan Jiasan in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時捻匪蜂起，振邦馳逐江北、皖、豫之間，擒石得珍於山套；

translations.literal: At that time Nian bandits swarmed everywhere; Zhenbang ranged between northern Jiangsu, Anhui, and Henan and captured Shi Dezhen in Shantao;
translations.idiomatic: As Nian bandits swarmed across the region, Zhenbang ranged between northern Jiangsu, Anhui, and Henan and captured Shi Dezhen in Shantao;

sentences.zh: 覆李大喜於符離；

translations.literal: he destroyed Li Daxi at Fuli;
translations.idiomatic: he destroyed Li Daxi at Fuli;

sentences.zh: 蹙孫葵心於茨河，歸德、陳州均肅清，以提督記名。

translations.literal: he pressed Sun Kuixin at Cihe; Guide and Chenzhou were both pacified, and he was placed on the list for regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: he cornered Sun Kuixin at Cihe; Guide and Chenzhou were both pacified, and he was placed on the list for promotion to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 九年，命代袁甲三督辦三省剿匪事，副都統伊興額副之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered to replace Yuan Jiasan in directing the three-province bandit-suppression effort, with Vice Commander-in-Chief Yi Xing'e as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he replaced Yuan Jiasan as director of the three-province suppression campaign, with Vice Commander-in-Chief Yi Xing'e as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 尋復命幫辦欽差大臣勝保軍，仍留督辦三省剿匪事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again ordered to assist Imperial Commissioner Senggelinqin's army while still retaining direction of the three-province suppression effort.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to assist Imperial Commissioner Senggelinqin while continuing to direct the three-province campaign.

sentences.zh: 澮北捻渠劉添福糾眾三萬圍團練苗沛霖營，振邦馳救，毀賊壘二十四。

translations.literal: The Nian leader Liu Tianfu north of the Hui River gathered thirty thousand men and besieged the militia camp of Miao Peilin; Zhenbang hurried to the rescue and destroyed twenty-four rebel forts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian leader Liu Tianfu north of the Hui River mustered thirty thousand men and besieged Miao Peilin's militia camp, Zhenbang hurried to the rescue and destroyed twenty-four rebel forts.

sentences.zh: 乘勝攻澮南，陣斬賊酋任乾，夷其圩，授雲南提督。

translations.literal: Pressing his advantage he attacked south of the Hui River, killed the rebel chief Ren Qian in battle, leveled his stockade, and was appointed regional commander of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing his advantage south of the Hui River, he killed the rebel chief Ren Qian in battle, leveled his stockade, and was appointed regional commander of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 蒙城王家圩諸圩聞任乾死，俱乞降，獨淝南板橋集賊陸連科負隅久抗。

translations.literal: When the stockades around Wangjia Stockade in Mengcheng heard of Ren Qian's death they all begged to surrender; only the rebel Lu Lianke at Banqiao Market south of the Fei River held out stubbornly for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Ren Qian's death, the stockades around Wangjia Stockade in Mengcheng all sued for surrender; only the rebel Lu Lianke at Banqiao Market south of the Fei River held out stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 振邦設計招降黃家圩，李華東為內應，擒陸連科誅之，淝南北六十餘圩悉就撫。

translations.literal: Zhenbang devised a plan to induce the surrender of Huangjia Stockade, with Li Huadong as an inside agent; Lu Lianke was captured and executed, and more than sixty stockades north and south of the Fei River all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenbang engineered the surrender of Huangjia Stockade with Li Huadong as an inside agent, captured and executed Lu Lianke, and brought more than sixty stockades north and south of the Fei River to submission.

sentences.zh: 六月，賊陷定遠，振邦馳援，破賊於宿州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month rebels took Dingyuan; Zhenbang hurried to relieve it and defeated the rebels at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, when rebels took Dingyuan, Zhenbang hurried to relieve the city and defeated them at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊竄固鎮，破之於方家坎渡口。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Guzhen, and he defeated them at the Fangjiakan crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels fled to Guzhen, he defeated them at the Fangjiakan crossing.

sentences.zh: 孫葵心竄唐家寨，窺濟寧，截擊之，賊退走。

translations.literal: Sun Kuixin fled to Tangjia Stockade and eyed Jining; Zhenbang intercepted him and the rebels retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kuixin fled to Tangjia Stockade and threatened Jining; Zhenbang cut him off and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔袁甲三代勝保為欽差大臣，振邦專任徐、宿剿匪事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year an edict made Yuan Jiasan replace Senggelinqin as imperial commissioner, and Zhenbang was placed solely in charge of suppression in Xuzhou and Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Yuan Jiasan replaced Senggelinqin as imperial commissioner, and Zhenbang was given sole charge of suppression in Xuzhou and Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 捻匪屢窺徐、宿，其老巢袁、徐兩圩跨澮南、河北，振邦進剿，連破其衝要臨渙、韓村、趙家海、張圩，餘多自拔就撫。

translations.literal: Nian bandits repeatedly probed Xuzhou and Suzhou; their main lairs, the Yuan and Xu stockades, straddled the Hui River north and south; Zhenbang advanced in suppression, successively broke their key positions at Linhuan, Hancun, Zhaojiahai, and Zhang Stockade, and most of the rest surrendered on their own.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian repeatedly probed Xuzhou and Suzhou; their main bases, the Yuan and Xu stockades, straddled the Hui River; Zhenbang advanced against them, took Linhuan, Hancun, Zhaojiahai, and Zhang Stockade in succession, and most of the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遂渡澮河攻袁圩。

translations.literal: He then crossed the Hui River to attack Yuan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed the Hui River to attack Yuan Stockade.

sentences.zh: 捻酋劉添福自豫回竄，擊敗之，再破之褚莊、邱家圩、檀城，五戰皆捷，殲賊六千有奇，擒其酋任護、任大牛。

translations.literal: The Nian chief Liu Tianfu fled back from Henan; Zhenbang defeated him, again defeated him at Chuzhuang, Qiujia Stockade, and Tancheng, won all five battles, destroyed more than six thousand rebels, and captured the chiefs Ren Hu and Ren Daniu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian chief Liu Tianfu fled back from Henan, Zhenbang defeated him, then beat him again at Chuzhuang, Qiujia Stockade, and Tancheng; he won all five battles, killed more than six thousand rebels, and captured the chiefs Ren Hu and Ren Daniu.

sentences.zh: 東路捻匪擾宿遷、睢寧，振邦戰於苗村，大破之。

translations.literal: Nian bandits on the eastern front harassed Suqian and Suining; Zhenbang fought at Miaocun and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Nian bandits on the eastern front raided Suqian and Suining; Zhenbang fought them at Miaocun and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 閏三月，偕田在田克閻圩，擒任虎、鄧三摩等誅之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month he joined Tian Zaitian in capturing Yan Stockade and captured and executed Ren Hu, Deng Sanmo, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month he joined Tian Zaitian in taking Yan Stockade and executed Ren Hu, Deng Sanmo, and others.

sentences.zh: 复破援賊，擒李大喜。

translations.literal: He again defeated relieving rebels and captured Li Daxi.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the relief column again and captured Li Daxi.

sentences.zh: 四月，連克澮南解溝、五溝、任圩賊巢，斬賊目李四喜、任友得三十餘名，收撫童亭、藕池四十二圩。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he successively captured the rebel lairs at Jiegou, Wugou, and Ren Stockade south of the Hui River, beheaded more than thirty rebel officers including Li Sixi and Ren Youde, and brought forty-two stockades at Tongting and Ouchi to submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he took the rebel bases at Jiegou, Wugou, and Ren Stockade south of the Hui River in succession, beheaded more than thirty rebel officers including Li Sixi and Ren Youde, and brought forty-two stockades at Tongting and Ouchi to submission.

sentences.zh: 五月，會攻袁圩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he joined in the assault on Yuan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he joined the assault on Yuan Stockade.

sentences.zh: 捻酋劉添祥等大舉來援，分軍擊之；

translations.literal: The Nian chiefs Liu Tianxiang and others came in force to relieve it, and he divided his army to strike them;
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian chiefs Liu Tianxiang and others marched in force to relieve the stockade, he split his army to meet them;

sentences.zh: 而永城捻萬餘直趨童亭，窺孫甿大營，振邦令副將龔耀倫擊敗其眾，擒捻首趙學煥等。

translations.literal: meanwhile more than ten thousand Nian from Yongcheng marched straight on Tongting and threatened Sun Mian's great camp; Zhenbang ordered Deputy Commander Gong Yaolun to defeat them and captured the Nian chief Zhao Xuehuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: while more than ten thousand Nian from Yongcheng marched on Tongting and threatened Sun Mian's main camp; Zhenbang sent Deputy Commander Gong Yaolun to defeat them and captured the Nian chief Zhao Xuehuan and others.

sentences.zh: 七月，拔蒙城西洋集賊圩十四。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he captured fourteen rebel stockades at Xiyangji in Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he took fourteen rebel stockades at Xiyangji in Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 潁、亳捻首姜台凌等北竄澮南，扼險截擊，擒賊目百餘。

translations.literal: The Nian chiefs Jiang Tailing and others from Ying and Bo fled north into the region south of the Hui River; he seized strategic points to intercept them and captured more than a hundred rebel officers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian chiefs Jiang Tailing and others from Ying and Bo fled north across the Hui River, he seized the passes to cut them off and captured more than a hundred rebel officers.

sentences.zh: 尋因傷發，請假回籍醫治，允之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his old wounds reopened and he asked for leave to return home for treatment; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His old wounds soon reopened, and he was granted leave to return home for treatment.

sentences.zh: 十一年，命督練民團防堵登、萊、青三府，振邦病未已，疏辭防堵，請專任團練，報可。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was ordered to supervise militia training and coastal defense in Deng, Lai, and Qing prefectures; Zhenbang was still ill, memorialized to decline coastal defense, and asked to be put solely in charge of militia training; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was ordered to train militia and guard the coast in Deng, Lai, and Qing; still ill, Zhenbang asked to be relieved of coastal defense and put solely in charge of militia training, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，命來京候簡。

translations.literal: That winter he was ordered to come to the capital to await appointment.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was ordered to the capital to await a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，勝保奏調振邦幫辦皖、豫軍，為山東所留，不果行。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Senggelinqin memorialized to transfer Zhenbang to assist the Anhui and Henan armies, but Shandong retained him and the move did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, Senggelinqin asked to transfer Zhenbang to the Anhui and Henan fronts, but Shandong kept him and the move never happened.

sentences.zh: 二年，僧格林沁調統前軍，從攻淄川、白蓮池，援蒙城。

translations.literal: In the second year Sengge Rinchen took command of the vanguard and Zhenbang followed in attacking Zichuan and Bailianchi and in relieving Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he served under Sengge Rinchen's vanguard in the attacks on Zichuan and Bailianchi and the relief of Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，從破捻酋張總愚於湖北隨州。

translations.literal: In the third year he took part in defeating the Nian chief Zhang Zongyu at Suizhou in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he helped defeat the Nian chief Zhang Zongyu at Suizhou in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 四年，以疾告歸，未幾疾愈，留督軍青、萊，移扼張秋河防。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he asked to retire home on grounds of illness; soon afterward he recovered and remained to command troops in Qing and Lai, then moved to hold the defenses along the Zhangqiu River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he went home ill; he soon recovered and stayed on to command troops in Qing and Lai, then moved to guard the Zhangqiu River line.

sentences.zh: 六年，會剿直隸梟匪，賊降复叛，褫翎頂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he joined in suppressing outlaw bandits in Zhili; the rebels surrendered and then rebelled again, and his insignia was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the campaign against outlaw bandits in Zhili; when the rebels surrendered and then rose again, his insignia was stripped.

sentences.zh: 尋破賊夏津，復之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he defeated the rebels at Xiajin and had his honors restored.
translations.idiomatic: He soon defeated the rebels at Xiajin and had his honors restored.

sentences.zh: 五年，西捻平，補直隸提督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the western Nian were pacified, he was appointed regional commander of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: When the western Nian were pacified in the fifth year, he was appointed regional commander of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，調湖北。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he was transferred to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Guangxu he was transferred to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 九年，以傷發回籍，未幾，卒於家，賜卹，諡剛勇。

translations.literal: In the ninth year his old wounds reopened and he returned home; soon afterward he died at home, was granted a pension, and was given the posthumous title Gangyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year his old wounds reopened and he went home; he soon died there, and the court granted a pension and the posthumous title Gangyong.

sentences.zh: 邱聯恩，字偉堂，福建同安人，浙江提督良功子。

translations.literal: Qiu Lian'en, styled Weitang, was a native of Tong'an in Fujian and the son of Zhejiang Regional Commander Liang Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Lian'en, courtesy name Weitang, came from Tong'an in Fujian and was the son of Zhejiang Regional Commander Liang Gong.

sentences.zh: 襲男爵，授乾清門侍衛。

translations.literal: He inherited the rank of baron and was appointed a guardsman of the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's barony and was appointed a guardsman of the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 道光二十三年，出為直隸通州協副將，調河間協。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Daoguang, on leaving the capital, he became deputy commander of the Tongzhou garrison in Zhili and was transferred to the Hejian garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Daoguang he left the capital as deputy commander of the Tongzhou garrison in Zhili and was transferred to the Hejian garrison.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，從勝保剿粵匪於靜海李家莊，擊敗之，又破樑頭、孫家莊賊營，擢南陽鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he followed Senggelinqin in suppressing Cantonese rebels at Lijia Village in Jinghai, defeated them, and again broke rebel camps at Liangtou and Sunjia Village; he was promoted to commander-in-chief of the Nanyang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he followed Senggelinqin against the Cantonese rebels at Lijia Village in Jinghai, routed them, and broke their camps at Liangtou and Sunjia Village; he was promoted to commander-in-chief of the Nanyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 剿光州捻匪，擒其渠丁心田，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He suppressed Nian bandits in Guangzhou and captured their leader Ding Xintian; he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the Nian in Guangzhou, captured their leader Ding Xintian, and was awarded a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 五年，捻首李世林敗死，其黨易添富糾汝陽、息縣諸匪，戕烏龍集州判，陷息縣，據光山。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Nian chief Li Shilin was defeated and killed; his follower Yi Tianfu rallied bandits from Ruyang, Xixian, and elsewhere, killed the subprefect at Wulongji, took Xixian, and held Guangshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Nian chief Li Shilin was killed in defeat; his follower Yi Tianfu rallied bandits from Ruyang, Xixian, and elsewhere, murdered the subprefect at Wulongji, seized Xixian, and occupied Guangshan.

sentences.zh: 聯恩督兵圍攻，賊宵遁，追擊，大破之，斃賊千餘，擒斬王黨、黃五雷等。

translations.literal: Lian'en directed troops in siege; the rebels fled by night, he pursued and inflicted a great defeat, killing more than a thousand rebels and capturing and executing Wang Dang, Huang Wulei, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Lian'en besieged them; the rebels fled by night, he pursued and routed them, killing more than a thousand rebels and capturing and executing Wang Dang, Huang Wulei, and others.

sentences.zh: 六年，皖捻首張洛行、龔瞎子等擾歸德，聯恩間道赴援，甫至，賊三路來撲，擊走之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Anhui Nian chiefs Zhang Luoxing, Gong Xiazi, and others harassed Guide; Lian'en took a bypath to relieve it, and as soon as he arrived the rebels attacked from three directions and he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Anhui Nian chiefs Zhang Luoxing and Gong Xiazi raided Guide; Lian'en took a roundabout route to relieve the city, and when the rebels attacked from three directions as soon as he arrived, he drove them off.

sentences.zh: 尋以進剿遲延，革職留營。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for delay in advancing the suppression, he was dismissed from office but kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon cashiered for slow progress in the campaign but kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 連破賊於穀熟集、界溝集，殲斃甚眾。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated the rebels at Gushuji and Jiegouji and killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: He won repeated victories at Gushuji and Jiegouji and killed a great many rebels.

sentences.zh: 進剿亳州五馬溝，大破之，殲賊千餘，擒賊目三十餘人，復原官。

translations.literal: Advancing to suppress Wumagou in Bozhou, he inflicted a great defeat, destroyed more than a thousand rebels, captured more than thirty rebel officers, and had his former rank restored.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against Wumagou in Bozhou, won a crushing victory, killed more than a thousand rebels, captured more than thirty rebel officers, and had his rank restored.

sentences.zh: 其冬，襄樊土匪起，入河南，陷鄧州、內鄉，聯恩馳擊，復其城，殲賊渠硃中立等，轄境得安。

translations.literal: That winter bandits rose in Xiangyang and Fancheng, entered Henan, and took Dengzhou and Neixiang; Lian'en hurried to attack, recovered the cities, destroyed the bandit leaders including Zhu Zhongli, and his jurisdiction was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That winter bandits rose in Xiangyang and Fancheng, entered Henan, and seized Dengzhou and Neixiang; Lian'en hurried to the scene, recovered both cities, destroyed the bandit leaders including Zhu Zhongli, and pacified his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 七年春，張洛行擁眾掠光州、固始，分據洪河南北。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year Zhang Luoxing led a host to plunder Guangzhou and Gushi and held positions on both banks of the Hong River.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year Zhang Luoxing led a large force against Guangzhou and Gushi and held both banks of the Hong River.

sentences.zh: 勝保大軍扼北岸，聯恩率兵千餘擊南岸，進攻方家集賊巢。

translations.literal: Senggelinqin's main force held the north bank; Lian'en led more than a thousand men against the south bank and advanced to attack the rebel lair at Fangjiaji.
translations.idiomatic: Senggelinqin's main force held the north bank while Lian'en led more than a thousand men against the south bank and advanced on the rebel base at Fangjiaji.

sentences.zh: 五月，諸軍合擊，聯恩直搗賊壘，破圩而入，乘勝追殺，焚洪河橋，兩岸賊皆潰，殲斃三千餘。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the armies joined in attack; Lian'en struck straight at the rebel fort, broke into the stockade, pursued and killed in the victory, burned the Hong River bridge, and rebels on both banks all collapsed; more than three thousand were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the armies attacked together; Lian'en stormed the rebel fort, broke into the stockade, pursued the fleeing enemy, burned the Hong River bridge, and routed the rebels on both banks, killing more than three thousand.

sentences.zh: 是役功最，賜號圖薩蘭巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In this campaign his merit was greatest, and he was granted the title Tusalang Batu'eru.
translations.idiomatic: His merit in this campaign was greatest, and he was awarded the title Tusalang Batooru.

sentences.zh: 九月，剿角子山捻匪，都統德楞阿敗賊確山，聯恩乘勝躡擊。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he suppressed Nian bandits at Jiaozishan; Commander-in-Chief Delinq'a defeated rebels at Queshan, and Lian'en followed up in victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he fought the Nian at Jiaozishan; Commander-in-Chief Delinq'a defeated rebels at Queshan, and Lian'en pressed the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 賊竄沁陽、嵩縣諸山中，搜捕數月，賊氛始清。

translations.literal: The rebels fled into the mountains of Qinyang, Songxian, and elsewhere; after months of search and capture the bandit threat was finally cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into the mountains around Qinyang and Songxian; after months of pursuit the region was finally pacified.

sentences.zh: 八年，回軍援固始，圍尋解。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he returned his army to relieve Gushi, and the siege was soon lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he marched back to relieve Gushi, and the siege was soon raised.

sentences.zh: 粵匪犯湖北，陷麻城。

translations.literal: Cantonese rebels invaded Hubei and took Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese rebels invaded Hubei and captured Macheng.

sentences.zh: 聯恩扼沙窩坊、虎頭關，防光山、商城一路。

translations.literal: Lian'en held Shawofang and Hutou Pass to guard the route toward Guangshan and Shangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lian'en held Shawofang and Hutou Pass to block the route toward Guangshan and Shangcheng.

sentences.zh: 十月，捻首孫葵心竄周家口，聯恩破之槐店。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Nian chief Sun Kuixin fled to Zhoujiakou; Lian'en defeated him at Huaidian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Nian chief Sun Kuixin fled to Zhoujiakou; Lian'en defeated him at Huaidian.

sentences.zh: 九年春，張洛行、龔瞎子復擾歸德，聯恩馳援，連破之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year Zhang Luoxing and Gong Xiazi again harassed Guide; Lian'en hurried to relieve it and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year Zhang Luoxing and Gong Xiazi raided Guide again; Lian'en hurried to the scene and beat them back repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 追至五溝營，賊分為二，其東竄者分兵擊潰於商水南，而自躡其西，孤軍獨進。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Wugouying, the rebels split in two; he detached troops to rout those fleeing east south of Shangshui, while he himself followed the western band alone with a solitary force.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them to Wugouying; when the rebels split in two, he detached troops to rout the eastern band south of Shangshui and pressed on alone after the western band.

sentences.zh: 巡撫恆福劾其追賊遲延，革職留營。

translations.literal: Governor Heng Fu impeached him for delay in pursuing the rebels; he was dismissed from office but kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Heng Fu impeached him for slow pursuit; he was cashiered but kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 賊犯西華，進擊解其圍。

translations.literal: When rebels attacked Xihua he advanced, attacked, and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked Xihua, he marched to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 追至舞陽北舞渡，日已暮，人馬皆未食，遇賊奮戰，進至殺虎橋，賊騎四面兜圍。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Beiwudu in Wuyang, night had fallen and neither men nor horses had eaten; he met the rebels and fought fiercely, advanced to Shahu Bridge, and rebel cavalry surrounded him on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them to Beiwudu in Wuyang; night had fallen and neither men nor horses had eaten when he met the rebels and fought on, reaching Shahu Bridge before rebel cavalry surrounded him on all sides.

sentences.zh: 聯恩身被重創，馬僕，步戰，手殺十餘賊，力竭，死之。

translations.literal: Lian'en was severely wounded, his horse fell, he fought on foot, killed more than ten rebels with his own hand, and when his strength was exhausted he died.
translations.idiomatic: Lian'en was badly wounded; his horse fell, he fought on foot, killed more than ten rebels with his own hands, and when his strength gave out he fell and died.

sentences.zh: 詔復原官，依提督陣亡例優恤，予騎都尉並一云騎尉世職，諡武烈。

translations.literal: An edict restored his former rank, granted preferential pension according to the precedent for a regional commander killed in battle, awarded a hereditary rank as Cavalry Commandant with one additional Yunqiwei, and gave him the posthumous title Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: The court restored his rank, granted the preferential pension due a regional commander killed in battle, awarded the hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Yunqiwei, and gave him the posthumous title Wulie.

sentences.zh: 南陽、同安並建專祠。

translations.literal: Dedicated shrines were built for him in both Nanyang and Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dedicated shrines were built for him in Nanyang and Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 無子，以族子嗣，炳忠襲男爵，炳義襲世職。

translations.literal: He had no son; a clansman was made his heir, Bingzhong inherited the barony, and Bingyi inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; a clansman succeeded him, Bingzhong inherited the barony, and Bingyi the hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 黃開榜，湖北施南人。

translations.literal: Huang Kaibang was a native of Shinan in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kaibang came from Shinan in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 初入湘軍，從塔齊布戰武、漢、蘄、黃間，累擢至都司。

translations.literal: When he first entered the Xiang Army, he fought under Ta Qibu in the Wuhan, Qichun, and Huangzhou regions, and was repeatedly promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first joined the Xiang Army and fought under Ta Qibu in the Wuhan, Qichun, and Huangzhou theaters, rising by successive promotions to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐七年，從勝保剿捻匪，克正陽關，擢游擊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianfeng he followed Sengbao in suppressing Nian bandits, captured Zhengyang Pass, and was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianfeng he served under Sengbao against the Nian, took Zhengyang Pass, and was promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 八年，偕副都統穆騰阿戰馬頭，開榜失利，褫翎頂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Vice Commander-in-Chief Muteng'a he fought at Matou; Kaibang suffered defeat and was stripped of his insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he fought at Matou alongside Vice Commander-in-Chief Muteng'a; Kaibang was defeated and stripped of his insignia.

sentences.zh: 复六安，加副將銜。

translations.literal: Lu'an was recovered, and he was granted the rank of deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu'an was recovered, he was granted the rank of deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，會豫軍毀潁上南照集賊巢，率水師攻蚌埠、長淮衛，戰七晝夜，獲賊船百餘，斃賊千餘，又焚賊舟糧，破懷遠水路諸卡，毀文昌閣賊壘，殺賊甚眾，賜號勤勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, joining Henan troops in destroying the rebel nest at Nanzhaoji in Yingshang, he led the naval force to attack Bengbu and Changhuaiwei; after seven days and nights of battle they captured more than a hundred rebel boats, killed more than a thousand rebels, burned rebel grain ships, broke the river checkpoints near Huaiyuan, destroyed the rebel fort at Wenchang Pavilion, killed very many rebels, and he was granted the title Qinyong Batu'eru.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he joined Henan troops in destroying the rebel stronghold at Nanzhaoji in Yingshang, then led the fleet against Bengbu and Changhuaiwei. After seven days and nights of fighting his forces captured more than a hundred rebel boats, killed over a thousand rebels, burned their grain ships, broke the river barriers near Huaiyuan, and destroyed the rebel fort at Wenchang Pavilion. For killing so many rebels he was awarded the title Qinyong Batooru.

sentences.zh: 合諸軍擊退援賊，直抵懷遠城下，先登，复懷遠，擢副將。

translations.literal: Joining with the other armies he drove back the relief rebels, pressed straight to the foot of Huaiyuan city, was first to scale the wall, recovered Huaiyuan, and was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the other armies in driving back the relief force, pressed to the foot of Huaiyuan, was first over the wall, and recovered the city; he was then promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 十年，袁甲三圍鳳陽，開榜會攻爐橋，捻首張洛行來援，會諸軍夾擊破之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Yuan Jiasan besieged Fengyang; Kaibang joined the attack on Luqiao; Nian chief Zhang Luoxing came to the relief; the combined armies defeated him in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Yuan Jiasan besieged Fengyang; Kaibang joined the assault on Luqiao. When Nian chief Zhang Luoxing came to the relief, the allied armies crushed him in a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 賊酋鄧正明潛乞降，覘府城虛實，開榜請聚師城外，示以兵威。

translations.literal: The rebel chief Deng Zhengming secretly sought to surrender while scouting the strength and weakness of the prefectural city; Kaibang requested that troops be massed outside the walls to display military might.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Deng Zhengming secretly offered to surrender while reconnoitering the prefectural city; Kaibang asked that troops be massed outside the walls to show force.

sentences.zh: 總兵張得勝誘擒賊首張隆，令縛獻賊酋悍黨十四人，磔於市。

translations.literal: Regional commander Zhang Desheng lured and captured rebel chief Zhang Long, had bound and presented fourteen of the rebel chiefs' fierce partisans, and had them dismembered in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Zhang Desheng lured and captured rebel chief Zhang Long, then had fourteen of the chiefs' fiercest followers bound and handed over to be dismembered in the market.

sentences.zh: 開榜梟張隆首示城賊，賊眾縛獻其酋乞降，誅悍者三百餘人，餘遣散歸業。

translations.literal: Kaibang displayed Zhang Long's head to the rebels in the city; the rebel masses bound and presented their chiefs begging to surrender; more than three hundred of the fierce were executed, and the rest were dispersed to return to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Kaibang displayed Zhang Long's head to the rebels inside the city; the rebel ranks then bound their chiefs and surrendered. More than three hundred of the most violent were executed, and the rest were disbanded to resume their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 功最，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: His merit was greatest; he was placed on the list for regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His contribution ranked first, and he was placed on the list for promotion to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 偕總兵田在田等破賊王家營，復清江浦，遂駐防。

translations.literal: Together with regional commander Tian Zaitian and others he defeated the rebels at Wangjiaying, recovered Qingjiangpu, and then garrisoned the place.
translations.idiomatic: Together with regional commander Tian Zaitian and others he routed the rebels at Wangjiaying, recovered Qingjiangpu, and remained to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 江寧大營潰，降賊薛成良叛入邵伯湖，開榜偕副將劉成元等毀賊船三百餘，殲賊殆盡，成良赴水死。

translations.literal: When the great camp at Jiangning collapsed, the surrendered rebel Xue Chengliang rebelled and entered Lake Shaobo; Kaibang together with deputy commander Liu Chengyuan and others destroyed more than three hundred rebel boats, wiped out the rebels almost entirely, and Chengliang drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the great Jiangning camp collapsed, the surrendered rebel Xue Chengliang rose again and fled into Lake Shaobo. Kaibang, with deputy commander Liu Chengyuan and others, destroyed more than three hundred rebel boats and nearly annihilated the force; Chengliang drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 加提督銜，授江西九江鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was granted the rank of provincial commander and appointed regional commander of the Jiujiang garrison in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the rank of provincial commander and appointed regional commander of the Jiujiang garrison in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，攻天長，疊平賊壘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he attacked Tianchang and successively leveled the rebel forts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he attacked Tianchang and one after another reduced the rebel forts.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，捻匪竄寶應，開榜督砲船擊走之，又敗賊於山陽、汊河。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Nian bandits raided Baoying; Kaibang directed gunboats to drive them off and also defeated rebels at Shanyang and Chahe.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, when Nian bandits raided Baoying, Kaibang led gunboats to drive them off and later defeated them at Shanyang and Chahe.

sentences.zh: 偕道員張富年破賊宿州觀音寺、仁和集，擒賊酋王春玉於邳州，拔貓兒窩賊柵。

translations.literal: Together with circuit intendant Zhang Funian he defeated rebels at Guanyin Temple and Renheji in Suzhou, captured rebel chief Wang Chunyu at Pizhou, and stormed the rebel stockade at Mao'erwo.
translations.idiomatic: With circuit intendant Zhang Funian he defeated rebels at Guanyin Temple and Renheji in Suzhou, captured rebel chief Wang Chunyu at Pizhou, and took the rebel stockade at Mao'erwo.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁劾開榜飾詞冒功，下漕運總督吳棠按究，得白，薦統徐、宿軍，兼節制水師。

translations.literal: Senggelinqin impeached Kaibang for embellishing his words and falsely claiming merit; the case was referred to Grand Canal Director Wu Tang for investigation; he was cleared, was recommended to command the Xuzhou and Suzhou armies, and was also given charge of the naval force.
translations.idiomatic: Senggelinqin accused Kaibang of exaggerating his reports and claiming credit falsely; the case was referred to Grand Canal Director Wu Tang for investigation. Kaibang was cleared, recommended to command the Xuzhou and Suzhou forces, and given charge of the fleet as well.

sentences.zh: 二年，攻長城賊堡，克之，收撫附近諸墟。

translations.literal: In the second year he attacked the rebel fort at Changcheng, captured it, and pacified the nearby abandoned villages.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he stormed the rebel fort at Changcheng, took it, and brought the nearby deserted hamlets back under control.

sentences.zh: 破郜家花園、孫甿賊巢，以提督記名。

translations.literal: He stormed the rebel nests at Gaojia Garden and Sun Meng, and was placed on the list for provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed the rebel nests at Gaojia Garden and Sun Meng and was placed on the list for promotion to provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 粵匪渡江北犯，開榜扼高郵，賊掠船渡湖犯天長，開榜往援，焚賊筏，軍於堤上。

translations.literal: Guangdong rebels crossed the Yangtze north to invade; Kaibang held Gaoyou; the rebels seized boats and crossed the lake to attack Tianchang; Kaibang went to the relief, burned their rafts, and encamped on the dike.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong rebels crossed the Yangtze to raid the north, Kaibang held Gaoyou. The rebels seized boats, crossed the lake, and struck at Tianchang; Kaibang hurried to the relief, burned their rafts, and encamped on the dike.

sentences.zh: 賊列陣以拒，開榜令副將龔雲福由陸路迎擊，參將陳浚家率砲劃潛出小河口，轉戰而前，與長城兵夾擊，破賊於三汊河，天長圍解。

translations.literal: The rebels formed battle lines to resist; Kaibang ordered deputy commander Gong Yunfu to meet them by the land route, and battalion commander Chen Junjia to lead gunboats out secretly from Xiaohekou; they fought forward in turn and, with the Changcheng troops in a pincer, defeated the rebels at Sanxhe River, and the siege of Tianchang was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels drew up in battle order to resist. Kaibang sent deputy commander Gong Yunfu to meet them by land and battalion commander Chen Junjia to slip gunboats out from Xiaohekou. Fighting forward in stages, they joined the Changcheng troops in a pincer at Sanxhe River, routed the rebels, and lifted the siege of Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 提督楊岳斌复​​江浦、浦口，開榜破七里洲賊壘，焚船六十餘艘。

translations.literal: Provincial commander Yang Yuebin recovered Jiangpu and Pukou; Kaibang stormed the rebel fort at Qilizhou and burned more than sixty boats.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial commander Yang Yuebin recovered Jiangpu and Pukou; Kaibang took the rebel fort at Qilizhou and burned more than sixty boats.

sentences.zh: 助攻九洑洲，拔之。

translations.literal: He joined the attack on Jiufu Island and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the assault on Jiufu Island and captured it.

sentences.zh: 開榜奉調赴臨淮，偕總兵普承堯平七里河岸賊壘。

translations.literal: Kaibang was ordered on transfer to Linhuai and, together with regional commander Pu Chengyao, pacified the rebel forts along the Qili riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Kaibang was transferred to Linhuai and, with regional commander Pu Chengyao, cleared the rebel forts along the Qili riverbank.

sentences.zh: 三年，率所部師船防通州，江寧平。

translations.literal: In the third year he led his own fleet to guard Tongzhou; Jiangning was pacified.
